title: Cement and Lime Charter calls for UK carbon capture commitment
summary: Cement and Lime Charter calls for UK carbon capture commitment
body_markdown:
**UK:** Representatives of the cement and lime industries signed the Cement and Lime Charter at the UK Parliamentary Cement and Lime Summit at the Palace of Westminster in London on 25 November 2026. Breedon, Holcim UK and CRH subsidiary Tarmac were among signatories to the charter, which calls on the government to invest in large-scale carbon capture and storage (CCS) projects like the Peak Cluster CCS pipeline project. The Peak Cluster project involves carbon capture installations at Breedon’s Hope cement plant, Holcim UK’s Cauldon cement plant and Tarmac’s Tunstead cement plant.


Peak Cluster CEO David Parkin said “This vital foundation industry is at a critical point and the government must provide greater certainty on carbon capture to safeguard British production, jobs and industrial capability. Put simply, there is no credible pathway to securing the long-term future of the UK’s cement and lime industry without CCS. Unless we decarbonise the industry, Britain faces a very real risk of losing production, jobs and investment overseas, while becoming increasingly reliant on imported materials.”
